Subject: Signing path and technical evidence sync for EU/UK pilot

Claire — thanks again for the time today. Per our call, want to align on a pragmatic signing cadence and the minimal technical evidence packet Medistate needs to close procurement for the EU+UK pilot. Quick proposal below and two asks.

Proposal (two-step signing):
- Step 1: Execute the core DPA (current redline v3 attached) to lock in contractual terms.
- Step 2: Execute UK Addendum via DocuSign, followed by delivery of the TIA evidence packet (operational artifacts + subprocessors list + residency attestation).

Two asks for next steps:
1) Confirm which Medistate reviewers need to sign the DocuSign envelope (legal + procurement? specific names).
2) Confirm whether the following items from our evidence matrix are sufficient for the UK Addendum: KMS/HSM attestation, subprocessor roster + access levels, network diagram showing data residency boundaries, and retention/egress controls.

Attached: Medistate_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, TIA_evidence_matrix.xlsx

If that sounds like a path, can we aim to: DPA signed by end of next week (May 10), DocuSign for UK Addendum queued same day, evidence packet delivered within 5 business days of DocuSign completion.

Happy to run a short 30-min ops sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Privacy & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@medistate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Medistate Legal <legal@medistate.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 13:34:10 +0100
Subject: Re: Signing path and technical evidence sync for EU/UK pilot

Jordan — thanks, this structure should work for us. A few clarifications from legal/procurement side: 

- Signers: Legal (Claire D'Souza) + Procurement (Tom Alvarez) will need DocuSign. I looped Tom on this thread.
- Evidence: Legal specifically called out the need for a KMS/HSM key custody attestation (we need whether keys are customer-controlled or Redwood-managed), an explicit list of subprocessors with country and role, and a network/dataflow diagram that shows where EU/UK subject data may traverse.
- Timeline: Procurement would like the DPA fully executed before their next board review on May 18 if possible.

We also need a short one-page summary of technical safeguards for procurement (they don't want to read the whole matrix). Can you produce that?

I'll open the DocuSign flow once you confirm signer emails.

—Claire
Claire D'Souza
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Medistate Health

Claire / Jordan — looping in operational details and owners. We can follow the two-step approach. A few concrete notes from our side: 

Operational evidence we will provide (initial packet):
- KMS/HSM attestation (documented by Security Ops) — confirms key custody model and rotation cadence.
- Latest subprocessor roster (CSV) with role, country, and whether live access is required.
- Network/dataflow diagram (high-level) with redaction-friendly markers for sensitive endpoints.
- Tokenization/kv-cache retention and purge policy summary (1 page).

Suggested cadence and owners: 
- DPA redline: Jordan to finalize by EOD May 3.
- Security artifacts: Security Ops to confirm KMS attestation by May 7 (owner: Marissa).
- Subprocessors CSV: Logan to assemble by May 5.
- One-page technical summary: Kimberly will draft and share by May 6.

DocuSign: once Jordan confirms final signer emails, we can publish the envelope. We recommend a two-envelope pattern to keep the UK Addendum linked but separate so evidence delivery can be tracked independently.

Attachment notes: we will not put control-plane diagrams with live IPs in the packet; everything will be redaction-friendly. If Medistate needs non-redacted artifacts for legal counsel review, we'll propose an NDA supplement and scheduled secure session.

Kimberly Park
VP, Legal Ops (Data Contracts)
Redwood Inference
